finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST parameter `feed` is passed directly to file_get_contents(), so any client can make the server fetch an arbitrary URL. The response is reduced to strlen, so the attack is largely blind.

trace.note: Branch gated only on REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST' and isset($_POST['feed']); no require_admin() or other auth
$_POST['feed'] flows unmodified into file_get_contents(), which accepts URL wrappers (http, https, ftp; file, php, phar when allow_url_fopen is on)
Only strlen($xml) is echoed, giving a size oracle (enough for port scanning and internal-service probing) rather than the body

finding.guards_checked: Authentication: none on this branch. Scheme allow-list: none. Host/IP allow-list or private-range block: none. Redirect control: none; file_get_contents follows redirects by default. DNS pinning: none. Expertise cases 04/12: this is the no-validation shape, not the validated-then-reparsed shape, so there is no check to bypass.

verdict.guard_found: none. import.php:11 gates only on REQUEST_METHOD and isset($_POST['feed']). require_admin() (import.php:4-9) is called only in the set_webhook branch at import.php:18, not on the feed branch. No scheme, host, or IP validation exists before file_get_contents at import.php:12.
verdict.reason: $_POST['feed'] at import.php:11 is attacker-controlled with no authentication, and it flows unmodified into file_get_contents() at import.php:12 with no closing guard, so any unauthenticated client can make the server fetch an arbitrary URL; the response is only strlen() at import.php:13, so the attack is blind as the candidate says.

finding.claim: The admin-only set_webhook parameter is passed to curl_init() and curl_exec() with no scheme or host restriction, so an admin, or anyone who obtains an admin session, can make the server request internal hosts or non-HTTP schemes.
finding.sink: import.php:20 curl_init($hook); executed at import.php:22 curl_exec($ch)

trace.note: require_admin() checks empty($_SESSION['is_admin']) and exits with 403 if unset
curl_init($hook) uses the raw string as the URL
curl_exec() performs the request from the server

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() at line 18 is a real server-side session gate for unauthenticated callers. No scheme allow-list, so curl may accept gopher://, file://, dict:// depending on build. No block for loopback, RFC1918, link-local (169.254.169.254 metadata), or localhost. CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION is unset (default off), which removes the redirect route but not the direct target. No DNS pinning applies because the target is never validated. Expertise cases 04/12: no check exists to bypass.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:18 (session gate on $_SESSION['is_admin'], exits 403). It is not a hostname, scheme, or IP allow-list, so it does not close the finding on its own. The refutation rests on the source check.
verdict.reason: Every trace line exists as described (import.php:17-22), but the source $_POST['set_webhook'] at import.php:19 is only reachable after require_admin() at import.php:18 rejects non-admin sessions with 403, so it is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege remote attacker. The claim therefore reduces to an admin-only SSRF, which falls outside this finding's scope. Separately, the unauthenticated $_POST['feed'] path at import.php:11-12 is a different sink and is not what this candidate describes.
